questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word 'lucid'.
questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means expressed clearly or easy to understand, so 'clear' is nearest in meaning.

questions.text: The word 'meticulous' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'impeccable'.
questions.explanation: 'Impeccable' means in accordance with the highest standards; faultless.

questions.text: 'Benevolent' is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly, i.e. kind.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'abundant'.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means existing or available in large quantities; plentiful.

questions.text: 'Candid' most nearly means honest and:
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward; frank.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'diligent'.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work.

questions.text: 'Vigilant' is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Vigilant' means keeping careful watch for possible danger; alert.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'coherent'.
questions.explanation: 'Coherent' means logical, consistent and orderly; easy to follow.

questions.text: 'Adequate' most nearly means sufficient and:
questions.explanation: 'Adequate' means satisfactory or acceptable in quality or quantity; enough.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'obsolete'.
questions.explanation: 'Obsolete' means no longer produced or used; out of date.

questions.text: 'Eloquent' is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Eloquent' means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'genuine'.
questions.explanation: 'Genuine' means truly what it is said to be; authentic.

questions.text: 'Inevitable' most nearly means certain to:
questions.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen; unavoidable.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'reluctant'.
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling and hesitant; disinclined.

questions.text: 'Transparent' in the sense of openness is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: Figuratively, 'transparent' means open and honest, without hidden motives.

questions.text: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'commence'.
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin or start.

questions.text: 'Abandon' most nearly means to give up:
questions.explanation: 'Abandon' means to give up completely or desert.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'proficient'.
questions.explanation: 'Proficient' means competent or skilled in doing something.

questions.text: 'Cumbersome' is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Cumbersome' means large, heavy, or difficult to handle; awkward.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'scarcity'.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcity' means shortage, so its opposite is 'abundance'.

questions.text: The word opposite in meaning to 'vague' is:
questions.explanation: 'Vague' means unclear, so the opposite is 'definite'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'frugal'.
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing with money, so the opposite is 'extravagant'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'optimist' is someone who is:
questions.explanation: An optimist expects good outcomes; a pessimist expects bad ones.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'temporary'.
questions.explanation: 'Temporary' means lasting a short time; opposite is 'permanent'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'humble' is someone who is:
questions.explanation: 'Humble' means modest; opposite is 'arrogant'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'expand'.
questions.explanation: 'Expand' means to make larger; opposite is 'contract' (make smaller).

questions.text: The opposite of 'transparent' is a material that is:
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' means see-through; 'opaque' means not see-through.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'courage'.
questions.explanation: 'Courage' means bravery; opposite is 'cowardice'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'permanent' is something that is:
questions.explanation: 'Permanent' means lasting forever; opposite is 'temporary'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'compulsory'.
questions.explanation: 'Compulsory' means required; opposite is 'voluntary'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'decrease' is to increase, or:
questions.explanation: 'Decrease' means to become smaller; opposite is 'increase'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'hostile'.
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly; opposite is 'friendly'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'barren' is land that is:
questions.explanation: 'Barren' means unable to produce life/crops; opposite is 'fertile'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'victory'.
questions.explanation: 'Victory' means a win; opposite is 'defeat'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'modern' is something that is:
questions.explanation: 'Modern' means present-day; opposite is 'ancient'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'artificial'.
questions.explanation: 'Artificial' means made by humans; opposite is 'natural'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'praise' is to criticise, or:
questions.explanation: 'Praise' means to express approval; opposite is 'blame'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'arid'.
questions.explanation: 'Arid' means very dry; opposite is 'wet' or 'humid'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'accept' is to refuse, or:
questions.explanation: 'Accept' means to receive willingly; opposite is 'reject'.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets the sentence: 'The new policy is a double-edged sword.'
options: It has both advantages and disadvantages
questions.explanation: A 'double-edged sword' is something that can help and harm at the same time.

questions.text: 'She decided to bury the hatchet with her rival.' This means she decided to:
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' means to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'He is the black sheep of the family.'
questions.explanation: A 'black sheep' is a member of a group regarded as a disgrace or odd one out.

questions.text: 'The teacher turned a blind eye to the noise.' This means the teacher:
questions.explanation: To 'turn a blind eye' means to deliberately ignore something.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'Don't count your chickens before they hatch.'
options: Don't plan on things that may not happen
questions.explanation: The proverb warns against assuming success before it actually occurs.

questions.text: 'It is raining cats and dogs.' This means:
questions.explanation: 'Raining cats and dogs' is an idiom meaning very heavy rain.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'He let the cat out of the bag.'
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret carelessly.

questions.text: 'She is feeling under the weather.' This means she is:
questions.explanation: 'Under the weather' means slightly unwell or sick.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'The ball is in your court now.'
options: It is your turn to act
questions.explanation: 'The ball is in your court' means it is now your responsibility to act.

questions.text: 'They saw eye to eye on the issue.' This means they:
questions.explanation: To 'see eye to eye' means to be in full agreement.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'The plan was a flash in the pan.'
questions.explanation: A 'flash in the pan' is a sudden success that is not repeated; brief.

questions.text: 'Stop beating about the bush.' This means stop:
questions.explanation: To 'beat about the bush' means to avoid coming to the point.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'A stitch in time saves nine.'
questions.explanation: The proverb means dealing with a problem early saves more work later.

questions.text: 'He is a jack of all trades.' This means he:
options: Is an expert in one thing
Can do many things reasonably well
questions.explanation: A 'jack of all trades' is someone skilled in many areas (often none mastered).

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'The news came like a bolt from the blue.'
questions.explanation: A 'bolt from the blue' is a sudden, unexpected event.

questions.text: 'She has an axe to grind with him.' This means she:
questions.explanation: To 'have an axe to grind' means to have a personal grievance or agenda.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.'
questions.explanation: The proverb means even bad situations have some positive aspect.

questions.text: 'He gave her the cold shoulder.' This means he:
questions.explanation: To 'give the cold shoulder' means to intentionally ignore someone.

questions.text: Select the option that best interprets: 'It cost him an arm and a leg.'
questions.explanation: 'Cost an arm and a leg' means extremely expensive.

questions.text: 'Birds of a feather flock together.' This means:
options: People associate with those similar to themselves
questions.explanation: The proverb means similar people tend to associate together.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Neither of the boys ___ present.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'was'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'The committee ___ divided on the issue.'
questions.explanation: When a collective noun acts as a single unit, it takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'One of the girls ___ missing.'
questions.explanation: The subject is 'one', which is singular, so 'is' is correct.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'The news ___ good today.'
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Each of the students ___ a book.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'Ten thousand naira ___ a lot of money.'
questions.explanation: Sums of money treated as a single amount take a singular verb.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Either John or his friends ___ to blame.'
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'friends' (plural).

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'The pair of shoes ___ expensive.'
questions.explanation: 'Pair' is the subject and is singular, so 'is' is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Everyone ___ invited to the party.'
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is an indefinite singular pronoun, taking 'is'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'The number of students ___ increasing.'
questions.explanation: 'The number' is singular, so 'is' is correct. ('A number of' would be plural.)

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Politics ___ a difficult subject.'
questions.explanation: 'Politics' (as a field of study) takes a singular verb.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'I ___ him yesterday.'
questions.explanation: A completed action in the past ('yesterday') takes the simple past 'saw'.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'She ___ to school every day.'
questions.explanation: Third person singular present simple takes 'goes'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'They have ___ their homework.'
questions.explanation: After 'have', the past participle 'done' is used.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'By next year, I ___ for ten years.'
questions.explanation: The future perfect 'will have worked' expresses completion before a future point.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'He ___ when the rain started.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous 'was walking' is used for an action in progress when another interrupted it.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'I have been living here ___ 2010.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in time (2010).

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'She has been waiting ___ two hours.'
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration of time (two hours).

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'The children ___ playing when I arrived.'
questions.explanation: 'Children' is plural, so the past continuous takes 'were'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'If I ___ rich, I would travel.'
questions.explanation: The unreal conditional uses the subjunctive 'were' for all persons.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'She runs FAST.'
questions.explanation: 'Fast' modifies the verb 'runs', so it is an adverb.

questions.text: In 'The quick brown fox', the word 'quick' is a(n):
questions.explanation: 'Quick' describes the noun 'fox', so it is an adjective.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'He spoke to the CROWD.'
questions.explanation: 'Crowd' is a thing/person named, so it is a noun.

questions.text: In 'She sang beautifully', the word 'beautifully' is a(n):
questions.explanation: 'Beautifully' modifies the verb 'sang', making it an adverb.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech: 'They will arrive SOON.'
questions.explanation: 'Soon' tells when, modifying the verb; it is an adverb of time.

questions.text: In 'The book ON the table is mine', 'on' is a:
questions.explanation: 'On' shows the relationship between 'book' and 'table', so it is a preposition.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech: 'AND' in 'I eat and sleep.'
questions.explanation: 'And' joins two words/clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.text: In 'She is a doctor', the word 'is' is a:
questions.explanation: 'Is' links the subject to its complement, so it is a linking verb.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech: 'WOW! That is amazing.'
questions.explanation: 'Wow!' expresses sudden emotion, making it an interjection.

questions.text: In 'He gave HER the book', 'her' is a:
questions.explanation: 'Her' is the indirect object here, functioning as an object pronoun.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'students' (plural).

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'The man, together with his sons, ___ arrived.'
questions.explanation: 'Together with' does not make the subject plural; the subject is 'the man' (singular).

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'I look forward to ___ from you.'
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to' in this phrase, the gerund 'hearing' is used.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'She is good ___ mathematics.'
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after 'good' is 'at'.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'He is interested ___ music.'
questions.explanation: 'Interested' takes the preposition 'in'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'We arrived ___ the station at noon.'
questions.explanation: 'Arrive at' is used for a specific point or place.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'She is afraid ___ dogs.'
questions.explanation: 'Afraid' takes the preposition 'of'.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'He complained ___ the noise.'
questions.explanation: 'Complain about' is the standard collocation.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'I prefer tea ___ coffee.'
questions.explanation: 'Prefer X to Y' is the correct structure.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'She is married ___ a doctor.'
questions.explanation: 'Married to' is the standard collocation.

questions.text: What type of sentence is: 'The sun rises in the east.'?
questions.explanation: It has one independent clause with one subject and predicate: a simple sentence.

questions.text: 'I wanted to go, but it was raining.' is a:
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' form a compound sentence.

questions.text: 'Although he was tired, he finished the work.' is a:
questions.explanation: It has one independent clause and one dependent clause: a complex sentence.

questions.text: 'She laughed and the baby clapped.' is a:
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'and' make a compound sentence.

questions.text: Identify the sentence type: 'Because it was late, we left, and we went home.'
questions.explanation: It has a dependent clause plus two independent clauses: compound-complex.

questions.text: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: Because he ran fast, he won.
He ran fast and he won the race.
He ran fast, but he lost.
questions.explanation: A simple sentence has one subject and a compound predicate; 'He ran fast and won' has one clause.

questions.text: 'Stop!' is which kind of sentence by function?
questions.explanation: 'Stop!' gives a command, so it is imperative.

questions.text: 'What a beautiful day!' is a(n) ___ sentence.
questions.explanation: It expresses strong emotion, so it is exclamatory.

questions.text: 'Did you finish the test?' is a(n) ___ sentence.
questions.explanation: It asks a question, so it is interrogative.

questions.text: 'The meeting starts at nine.' is a(n) ___ sentence.
questions.explanation: It makes a statement, so it is declarative.

questions.text: Identify the main clause in: 'When the bell rang, the students rushed out.'
questions.explanation: 'The students rushed out' can stand alone, so it is the main (independent) clause.

questions.text: In 'If you study hard, you will pass', the subordinate clause is:
questions.explanation: 'If you study hard' cannot stand alone; it is the subordinate (dependent) clause.

questions.text: A sentence that contains two or more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause is:
questions.explanation: That is the definition of a compound-complex sentence.

questions.text: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
questions.explanation: Direct speech needs a comma before the quote and a capital letter inside it.

questions.text: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence' (double c, double r).

questions.text: Select the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' has one c and double s.

questions.text: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'separate'.

questions.text: Select the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: 'Receive' follows the 'i before e except after c' rule.

questions.text: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'definitely'.

questions.text: Select the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: 'Accommodation' has double c and double m.

questions.text: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'government'.

questions.text: Select the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: 'Embarrass' has double r and double s.

questions.text: Choose the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Select the word that is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege' (no 'd').

questions.text: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Boys'' shows plural possessive (books of the boys).

questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I need to buy, eggs milk and bread.
I need, to buy eggs milk and bread.
I need to buy eggs milk and bread.
I need to buy eggs, milk, and bread.
questions.explanation: Items in a list are separated by commas.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses a semicolon?
options: He was tired; so he slept.
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two related independent clauses without a conjunction.

questions.text: Select the correct use of 'their', 'there' or 'they're'.
questions.explanation: 'They're' is the contraction of 'they are'.

questions.text: Which word completes the sentence correctly: 'It's ___ book.'
questions.explanation: 'Your' is the possessive adjective needed before the noun 'book'.

questions.text: How many vowel sounds are there in the English language?
questions.explanation: English has 20 vowel sounds (12 monophthongs and 8 diphthongs).

questions.text: How many consonant sounds are there in English?
questions.explanation: English has 24 consonant sounds.

questions.text: The word 'ship' contains which vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Ship' has the short vowel /ɪ/, as in 'sit'.

questions.text: The vowel sound in 'seat' is which type of sound?
questions.explanation: 'Seat' contains the long vowel /iː/.

questions.text: Which of these words contains a diphthong?
questions.explanation: 'Boy' contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

questions.text: The word 'chair' begins with which consonant sound?
questions.explanation: 'Chair' begins with the affricate /tʃ/.

questions.text: The final sound in 'sing' is which type of sound?
questions.explanation: 'Sing' ends with the velar nasal /ŋ/.

questions.text: Which word has the /θ/ (voiceless 'th') sound?
questions.explanation: 'Think' has the voiceless /θ/; 'this' and 'they' have voiced /ð/.

questions.text: The word 'zoo' begins with which type of sound?
questions.explanation: 'Zoo' begins with the voiced /z/.

questions.text: In 'church', the initial sound is a(n):
questions.explanation: The /tʃ/ in 'church' is an affricate.

questions.text: The sound /b/ in 'bat' is classified as a:
questions.explanation: /b/ is a bilabial plosive (stop).

questions.text: The sound /s/ in 'sun' is classified as which type?
questions.explanation: /s/ is a voiceless alveolar fricative.

questions.text: Which word contains the /ʒ/ sound (as in 'measure')?
questions.explanation: 'Vision' contains the voiced /ʒ/ sound.

questions.text: The 'l' sound in 'little' is classified as which type?
questions.explanation: /l/ is a lateral consonant, made with air flowing around the sides of the tongue.

questions.text: The word 'cat' contains how many consonant sounds?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' has two consonants (/k/ and /t/) and one vowel.

questions.text: In the word 'important', the primary stress falls on the:
questions.explanation: 'imPORtant' — stress is on the second syllable.

questions.text: Which syllable is stressed in 'education'?
questions.explanation: 'eduCAtion' — primary stress is on the third syllable 'ca'.

questions.text: The word 'record' is stressed differently depending on whether it is used as a noun or a verb. As a NOUN, the stress is on the:
questions.explanation: Nouns take first-syllable stress (REcord); verbs take second (reCORD).

questions.text: In 'photograph', the stressed syllable is:
questions.explanation: 'PHOtograph' — stress is on the first syllable.

questions.text: Which word has its stress on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: 'TEACHer' is stressed on the first syllable; the others on the second.

questions.text: The rise and fall of the pitch of the voice when speaking is called:
questions.explanation: Intonation is the variation in pitch across speech.

questions.text: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in poetry is called:
questions.explanation: Meter is the rhythmic pattern of stressed/unstressed syllables.

questions.text: Which of the following words is a homophone of 'write'?
questions.explanation: 'Write', 'right' and 'rite' all sound alike but differ in spelling/meaning.

questions.text: A word that has the same spelling but different meanings is a:
questions.explanation: A homograph is spelt the same but has different meanings (e.g. 'bank').

questions.text: 'Sea' and 'see' are examples of which type of words?
questions.explanation: They sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning: homophones.

questions.text: In a declarative statement, the intonation pattern is typically:
questions.explanation: Statements normally end with falling intonation.

questions.text: Yes/no questions typically end with ___ intonation.
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions use rising intonation at the end.

questions.text: In a passage, if an author describes a character as 'frugal', the character is:
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means economical and careful about spending.

questions.text: The primary purpose of a persuasive passage is to:
questions.explanation: Persuasive writing aims to convince or persuade the reader.

questions.text: In comprehension, the main idea of a passage is best found by:
options: Identifying the central point the writer makes
questions.explanation: The main idea is the central point or message of the passage.

questions.text: A summary of a passage should include which of these?
questions.explanation: A summary condenses a passage to its key points without copying.

questions.text: The word 'emigrate' means to move out of:
options: Leave one's country to live elsewhere
questions.explanation: 'Emigrate' means to leave one's country to settle in another.

questions.text: 'Immigrate' means to move into a country:
options: Enter and settle in a new country
questions.explanation: 'Immigrate' means to come into a country to live there.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'The lecture was so boring that most students ___ off.'
questions.explanation: 'Dozed off' is the correct phrasal verb meaning to fall asleep briefly.

questions.text: Select the correct option: 'He was accused ___ stealing.'
questions.explanation: 'Accused of' is the correct collocation.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'She was absorbed ___ her book.'
questions.explanation: 'Absorbed in' is the standard collocation.

questions.text: Select the correct option: 'The boys were divided ___ two groups.'
questions.explanation: 'Divided into' is the correct collocation.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'I am fed up ___ this noise.'
questions.explanation: 'Fed up with' is the standard expression.

questions.text: Select the correct option: 'He congratulated her ___ her success.'
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate someone on something' is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'The teacher insisted ___ punctuality.'
questions.explanation: 'Insist on' is the correct collocation.

questions.text: Select the correct option: 'We should always aim ___ excellence.'
questions.explanation: 'Aim at' is the standard collocation.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'candid' in: 'He gave a candid account of the event.'
questions.explanation: 'Candid' here means frank and truthful.

questions.text: In the sentence 'The drought devastated the crops', 'devastated' means:
questions.explanation: 'Devastated' means ruined or destroyed completely.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in italics: 'His ARGUMENT was compelling.'
questions.explanation: 'Compelling' means convincing and persuasive.

questions.text: The word 'scanty' in 'scanty rainfall' means:
questions.explanation: 'Scanty' means small or insufficient in amount; meagre.

questions.text: 'The officer was impartial in his judgment.' 'Impartial' means:
questions.explanation: 'Impartial' means fair and unbiased; neutral.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes: 'Her sudden wealth was ___ by envy among her peers.'
questions.explanation: 'Followed by' fits the context: wealth then envy.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'procrastinate'.
questions.explanation: 'Procrastinate' means to delay or postpone action.

questions.text: 'Ambiguous' most nearly means unclear or:
options: Having more than one possible meaning
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'concise'.
questions.explanation: 'Concise' means giving much information clearly in few words.

questions.text: 'Hostile' in 'a hostile environment' means:
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly, harsh, or adverse.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'exhausted'.
questions.explanation: 'Exhausted' means extremely tired.

questions.text: 'Vanish' most nearly means to disappear:
questions.explanation: 'Vanish' means to disappear suddenly.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'triumph'.
questions.explanation: 'Triumph' means a great victory or achievement.

questions.text: 'Audacious' most nearly means bold or:
questions.explanation: 'Audacious' means daring and bold.

questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to 'obstinate'.
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind.

questions.text: 'Serene' most nearly means calm and:
questions.explanation: 'Serene' means calm, peaceful, and untroubled.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'acquit'.
questions.explanation: 'Acquit' means to declare innocent; opposite is 'convict'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'attract' is to repel, or:
questions.explanation: 'Attract' means to draw toward; opposite is 'repel'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'assemble'.
questions.explanation: 'Assemble' means to gather; opposite is 'disperse'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'ancient' is something that is:
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old; opposite is 'modern'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'confess'.
questions.explanation: 'Confess' means to admit; opposite is 'deny'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'generous' is someone who is:
questions.explanation: 'Generous' means freely giving; opposite is 'stingy'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'applaud'.
questions.explanation: 'Applaud' means to show approval; opposite is 'boo'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'arrival' is the act of:
questions.explanation: 'Arrival' means coming; opposite is 'departure'.

questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to 'sorrow'.
questions.explanation: 'Sorrow' means sadness; opposite is 'joy'.

questions.text: The opposite of 'swift' is someone or something that is:
questions.explanation: 'Swift' means fast; opposite is 'slow'.

questions.text: Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: A question must end with a single question mark.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'I ___ my keys; I can't find them anywhere.'
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have lost' is used for a past action with present relevance.

questions.text: Select the correct form: 'By the time we arrived, the film ___.'
questions.explanation: Past perfect 'had started' is used for an action completed before another past action.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'Hardly had he left ___ it began to rain.'
questions.explanation: 'Hardly...when' is the correct correlative structure.
